description: THE period-end execution tool — process multiple IFRS calculations for a reporting period in one call (year-end, quarter-end, or month-end). One tool, three modes: (1) PLAIN BATCH (default): items + accountingPolicy → per-item results, every item's journal entries in one list, trial balance, and all financial statements. (2) SUMMARY: leave includeWorkings false (the default) for the compact ~200KB response; set includeWorkings:true only when step-by-step workings are needed (~600KB). (3) CLOSE: additionally pass entityProfile (fact flags) for a one-call period-end close — the response gains the applicability checklist, recommendedOrder, and a coverage analysis flagging any standard the profile implies but no item was supplied for (the checklist/coverage portion is free). REQUIRED: each item's `input` object must include an `id` field (e.g. { type:"ias37", input:{ id:"PROV-LEGAL-001", ...otherFields } }) — validated by the controller schema; stamped as Reference on every journal entry for that item. GROUP vs BATCH (G-1700): items of ONE entity → its separate statements; items of TWO OR MORE entities (input.entityId) + the group block (parent, entities[] with the control facts, intragroup rows) + previousPeriodBalances with row.entity → each entity's separate statements AND the consolidated set in one call (the IFRS 10 group cascade fed with the statements derived from the entities' own items). An ifrs10 item in a one-entity batch is refused. With the entities' statements already in hand, call the group cascade directly (ifr_calculate, elementType "group"). CASCADE TRACE: each item result carries `context.cascadeTrace` — every cross-standard chain evaluated (PRE satellite inputs + POST consequential standards), each with status "fired" or "skipped" and a skipReason when skipped. This is the per-item completeness record. MANDATORY CONSIDERATIONS: every item must address its tier-1 cascade considerations (data OR explicit denial evidence — impairmentIndicatorsPresent: false, deferredTaxAssessment enum, dismantlingEstimate: 0...); preflight validation rejects silent omissions and these judgement fields are EXCLUDED from auto-fill — collect the answers from the user (ifr_period_checklist lists them per standard under mandatoryConsiderations). INPUT COVERAGE: each item's data.ignoredInputs lists submitted fields the taken path did not use; affected items are rolled up in the batch-level ignoredInputsAlerts and each was AUTOMATICALLY flagged for quality check server-side. UNDECLARED FIELDS (G-1795): a field on an item that its standard does not declare is REFUSED before anything is calculated (FIELD_UNRECOGNISED, naming the field and the item) — the same answer ifr_batch_validate gives; nothing is silently ignored. input.entityId is the batch's entity dimension and is never refused. ACCOUNTING POLICY — build the accountingPolicy block BEFORE calling this tool. Always include at top level: functionalCurrencyIndicators (the IAS 21.9-11 facts the functional currency is derived from — G-2343; not functionalCurrency, which is stated only where the engine asks), presentationCurrency, reportingDate, previousReportingDate. Each standard that appears in items[] may also need its own policy block (measurement model, cost formula, presentation method...). Do NOT guess these: the ifr_schema response for a standard carries `batchAccountingPolicySchema` with that standard's required policy fields and their allowed values, generated from the engine itself. For the whole table in one place, read ifrs://reference/accounting-policy-choices. RATE GOVERNANCE: discount/interest rates are explicit inputs — preflight rejects (free, no credits) any item whose required rate is missing. Supply rates per item, or once for the whole batch via accountingPolicy.reportingInterestRates { corporateBondYield (IAS 19.83), riskFreePreTax (IAS 37.47 — provisions, dismantling/restoration), governmentBondYield, riskFreePostTax }. Lease rates (IFRS 16.26 implicit rate / IBR) and instrument EIRs are lease/instrument-specific — always per item, never a policy default. Which rate type applies where: read ifrs://reference/discounting-and-interest-rate-guide; each schema response lists its rateRequirements. ASSEMBLY WORKFLOW: (1) IDENTIFY — for each item whose standard is not explicitly named, call ifr_route_event in parallel to resolve the slug. (2) FREE VALIDATE LOOP — assemble all items[] plus accountingPolicy, then call ifr_batch_validate (free). Fix all reported errors and repeat until allValid: true. Never call ifr_period_end_batch until allValid is true — the validate loop costs zero credits. (3) CALCULATE — once allValid: true, submit to ifr_period_end_batch in the DEFAULT mode (do NOT pass mode). The default mode is the one that assembles and returns the consolidated output; only it returns the trial balance, the financial statements and the workbook link. It returns every item's journal entries in one list (batchJournalEntries), trial balance grouped by XBRL section (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, PL, OCI), financial statements, cash flow statement and disclosure notes. DOWNLOAD (default mode only): the response includes calculationSheetsUrl — a direct link to an 8-sheet Excel workbook (Movements in SoFP, Financial Performance, OCI, Movements in Equity, Cashflow, Disclosure Checklist, Journal Entries, Movements Balance) valid for 24 hours. It is fetched with the IFRS token (Authorization: Bearer <token>) and each download costs 15 credits; opened in a browser without the token it answers 401 — so do not hand it to the user as a link to click: fetch it yourself if you can send the header, or tell the user the workbook is waiting under 'Downloadable workbooks' at https://ifrcoworker.app/#downloads (signed in). RESILIENCE FALLBACK — mode: "partial": pass this ONLY to stop one bad item rejecting the whole batch. It validates-then-calculates each item independently and returns per-item results in results[i].result.data (status "ok" | "validation_error" | "calculation_error"); it does NOT assemble or return batchJournalEntries, trialBalance, financialStatements, cashFlowStatement, disclosureNotes, crossChecks/selfCheck or calculationSheetsUrl, and it persists no workbook. Use it to isolate the failing item, fix that item, then re-run the whole batch in the default mode to obtain the consolidated statements and the download link. SIZE CONTROL: the response defaults to compact. includeWorkings, includeXbrlEnrichment and exportXbrl each enlarge it — read their field descriptions in this tool's input schema before setting any of them. The trial balance always carries xbrlElement, xbrlSection and xbrlLabel regardless of those flags. DELIVERY TO A GOOGLE SHEET — BEFORE you call this tool, ask the user explicitly whether they want the output (the .csv journal entries AND the financial statements) delivered back into a Google table (Google Sheet), or just returned inline. If the user says yes: FIRST verify that you (the calling agent) have a working Google Sheets / Drive connector and can actually write to it — perform a real write test (create or append a throwaway cell), not just a capability assumption. If no Google Sheets connector is connected or the write test fails, tell the user and DO NOT run the batch — this call is billable and the result could not be delivered where requested; resolve the connection first. Only once the export path is confirmed: call this tool with exportJournalCsv: true, then write the returned journalCsvFile content and the financialStatements into the Google Sheet. BATCH SIZE GUIDANCE: aim for ≤50 economic events (line items) per call to stay within context window limits and receive full workings. Above 50 items the response grows rapidly; above 200 items you will very likely receive a compact response (workings and disclosures stripped, journal entries + statements + trial balance remain intact). If the user has more than 50 economic events, split into multiple calls of ≤50 items each, then merge the trial balances and journal entry lists in your context — do not attempt a single call with 200+ items unless the user explicitly accepts compact output.

accountingPolicy.description: REQUIRED entity-wide accounting policy declaration. Must include at top level: entityId, entityIdentifiers, functionalCurrencyIndicators, presentationCurrency, reportingDate, expenseAnalysis. functionalCurrencyIndicators (G-2343) — the IAS 21.9-11 facts the functional currency is DERIVED from: { currencyOfSalesRevenue, currencyOfCompetitiveForces, currencyOfLabourMaterialAndOtherCosts } (IAS 21.9, ISO 4217) each with its <name>Predominates boolean (false = no one currency predominates — omit the currency); where the three name one currency it is the functional currency and nothing else is asked; otherwise currencyOfFinancingActivities / currencyOfOperatingReceipts (21.10, with their flags) and, for a foreign operation (accountingPolicy.isForeignOperation true, parentFunctionalCurrency), the four 21.11 booleans are required. functionalCurrency is NOT stated where the facts settle it (refused DERIVED_FIELD); only where the engine asks (21.9 split and 21.10-11 leave none or several of the 21.9 currencies), and then one of the 21.9 currencies. Every item that reads the functional currency receives the derived one; IAS 21 and IFRS 1 items receive the facts. expenseAnalysis (G-1946) — BY_NATURE | BY_FUNCTION, no default: the analysis of expenses in profit or loss (IAS 1.99) — by nature (IAS 1.102) or by function (IAS 1.103); by function every item posting an operating expense states its expenseFunction. entityIdentifiers = { lei?, taxNumber?, nationalCompanyId? } — the reporting entity's identifiers (IAS 1.51(a)); at least one must be a non-empty string, none is format-checked. They are written to the workbook's XBRL Report Info, and the XBRL instance identifies the entity by the LEI, else the tax number, else the national company id (only an LEI is ESEF-fileable). Batch level only — not carried into items. entityId (G-1699) names the reporting entity whose books this batch closes — one batch is one entity: every journal and trial-balance line carries it as `entity`, an item stating a different entityId is refused (never merged) unless the batch is a GROUP batch (see `group`, G-1700): there accountingPolicy.entityId names the parent, every entity's items carry their own input.entityId, and the consolidation adjustments carry the group entity they relate to (counterpartyEntity on intragroup rows). An IFRS 10 item in a one-entity batch is refused. isInvestmentEntity (G-1752) — boolean: is the reporting entity an investment entity as defined in IFRS 10 (10.27)? REQUIRED only in a one-entity batch whose bank lines state PROCEEDS_FROM_ / PAYMENTS_FOR_CHANGES_IN_OWNERSHIP_WITHOUT_LOSS_OF_CONTROL (IAS 7.42A); true refuses those values — an investment entity's subsidiary at fair value through profit or loss is an investment, so the flow is investing: use PROCEEDS_FROM_SALE_ / PURCHASE_OF_EQUITY_OR_DEBT_INSTRUMENTS_OF_OTHER_ENTITIES (7.16(c)/(d)). normalOperatingCycle (G-1863 D3) — { clearlyIdentifiable: true, lengthDays } or { clearlyIdentifiable: false }: the entity's normal operating cycle, ONE fact about the entity (IAS 1.68, 1.70; not clearly identifiable → IAS 1.68 assumes twelve months). Filled into every IAS 41 and IFRS 15 item that does not state it; read only where an item is realised or settled more than twelve months after the reporting date (IAS 1.66(a), 1.69(a)); not stated, twelve months are assumed (IAS 1.68) and the item's basis says so. Standard-specific policy choices are required per standard block when that standard appears in items (IFRS requires same-class/same-category consistency — IAS 16.36, IAS 2.25). Format: { entityId, entityIdentifiers: { lei }, functionalCurrencyIndicators: { currencyOfSalesRevenue: "EUR", currencyOfSalesRevenuePredominates: true, currencyOfCompetitiveForces: "EUR", currencyOfCompetitiveForcesPredominates: true, currencyOfLabourMaterialAndOtherCosts: "EUR", currencyOfLabourMaterialAndOtherCostsPredominates: true }, presentationCurrency, reportingDate, ias2: { costFormula }, ias16: { measurementModel, byClass?: {BUILDINGS: "REVALUATION"} }, ias38: { measurementModel }, ias40: { measurementModel }, ifrs6: { explorationCostPolicy }, reportingInterestRates?: { corporateBondYield: 0.049, governmentBondYield: 0.038, riskFreePreTax: 0.042, riskFreePostTax: 0.034 } }. reportingInterestRates is optional — declare entity-level rate defaults once; engine injects: corporateBondYield → IAS 19 discountRateCorporateBond, riskFreePreTax → IAS 37 discountRatePreTax AND the IAS 37.47 rate of the dismantling / restoration provisions the asset standards cascade to IAS 37 (IAS 16 / IAS 40 dismantlingDiscountRate, IFRS 6 / IFRS 16 restorationDiscountRate — differs from the lease IBR). Item-level values always override. Resolution order (most specific wins): 1) item.input value, 2) policy[standard].byClass/byCategory/byType[classValue], 3) policy[standard].default, 4) reportingInterestRates defaults.

cashBalances.description: G-1744 — REQUIRED in every batch (refused when absent; an entity holding no bank account and no cash box states []): one row per bank account and cash box, its opening and closing balance. Balances are stated in the account's OWN currency, as the bank statement shows them (G-1759); a foreign-currency row is translated into the functional currency at the rates of the batch's IAS 21 item retranslating that cash (rateAtPreviousReportingDate, closingRateAtReportingDate — IAS 21.23(a)), and both figures are published with the rate and its source. The batch foots each row in the functional currency — opening + Σ the general journal's lines on it (debit − credit) + IAS 21's retranslation of a foreign-currency balance (IAS 21.23(a), 21.28) = closing — and refuses a row that does not, by account, with each figure and the difference. A general-journal cash line, or an IAS 21 item retranslating cash held (monetaryItemType CASH, on the account its cashAccount names — G-1786), whose account has no row is refused before anything is calculated; so is a foreign-currency row with no IAS 21 item for that cash. Where two rows share entity, account and currency, the IAS 21 item states its cashAccountId too (G-1760). G-1785: a general-journal entry in a foreign transactionCurrency is posted translated at its spotRateAtTransactionDate on its transactionDate (IAS 21.21-22). G-1787 (RECOMMENDED, owner to confirm): a foreign-currency row foots first in its own currency (opening + the general journal's foreign amounts on it = closing, inAccountCurrency); its IAS 21 retranslation is DERIVED — foreignCurrencyAmount from the row's openingBalance, the receipts and payments from the general journal's lines on it, each at its own rate — so the item states neither cashMovements nor a different foreignCurrencyAmount (refused). The response publishes cashReconciliation (group: separateStatements[entityId].cashReconciliation): the footing per account, and the IAS 7.45 reconciliation of the cash flow statement (direct method, from the bank lines' cashFlowLineItem) to the balances. With it, settlementMatching (G-1745): per IAS 7 line item, the bank lines against the standards' settlements due — settled, outstanding or over-settled within the period.

account.description: The cash account — one of the general journal's cash and cash-equivalent accounts (isCashEquivalent in the tag map).
enum: Restricted Cash — cash and cash equivalents

cashAccountId.description: Short code of the bank account or cash box. REQUIRED where two rows of one entity share the account and currency; every general-journal cash line on them then states the same code (entries[i].cashAccountId).

closingBalance.description: Balance at reportingDate, in the account's own currency (G-1759), on the same basis as openingBalance and the general journal's bank entries: the bank statement balance where liabilities are derecognised on the settlement date (IFRS 9 B3.1.2A), net of payments initiated but not yet debited where the entity elects B3.3.8, card payments blocked on the account but not yet booked by the bank included (G-2303); a foreign-currency balance is translated at the IAS 21 item's closingRateAtReportingDate (its estimatedSpotRate where the currency is not exchangeable, IAS 21.19A). In the functional currency it must equal opening + the general journal's entries on the account + the IAS 21.28 retranslation, or the batch is refused naming the account, both figures, the rates and the difference.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency the account is held in. An IAS 21 retranslation of cash held is matched by its cashAccount (G-1786), its foreignCurrency (and its cashAccountId, G-1760); a foreign-currency general-journal line by its transactionCurrency (G-1785).

entity.description: The entityId whose account this is. REQUIRED on every row of a group batch; in a one-entity batch, stated, it must be accountingPolicy.entityId.

openingBalance.description: Balance at previousReportingDate as the bank statement / cash-box count shows it — on the same basis as the general journal's bank entries: an entity that derecognises paid liabilities when it initiates an electronic payment (IFRS 9 B3.3.8, elected per payment system, B3.3.10) states the balance net of payments initiated but not yet debited, card payments blocked on the account but not yet booked by the bank included (G-2303) — in the ACCOUNT'S OWN currency (`currency`), G-1759. For a foreign-currency account the engine derives the functional amount at the previous closing rate of the batch's IAS 21 item retranslating that cash (its rateAtPreviousReportingDate, IAS 21.23(a)); a foreign-currency row without such an item is refused. 0 is an answer; absence is refused.

csvFilename.description: Filename for the CSV export, e.g. "journal_entries_2025.csv". Used as journalCsvFile.filename; defaults to journal_entries_<reportingDate>.csv.

entityProfile.description: OPTIONAL close mode — entity fact flags (hasInventory, hasPPE, hasLeases, hasFinancialInstruments, hasDefinedBenefitPlan, isGroup, isListed, incomeTaxApplicable, ...; same shape as ifr_period_checklist). When provided, the response additionally includes the applicability checklist, recommendedOrder, and a coverage analysis (missingApplicableStandards = standards the profile implies but no item supplied; unexpectedStandards = supplied but not implied). Use this for a one-call period-end close with a completeness gate. Omit for a plain batch run.

exportJournalCsv.description: When true, the response includes a journalCsvFile object { filename, mimeType, encoding, rowCount, byteLength, content, saveInstruction } with XBRL-enriched journal entries. Write `content` to `filename` to save the .csv. Costs 25 extra credits.

exportXbrl.description: When true, adds an xbrlFacts array to the response — a flat list of all monetary facts with full XBRL context: element (ifrs-full:...), periodType (instant|duration), balance (debit|credit), value, currency, decimals (0), namespace, taxonomyYear. The context block includes period dates from reportingDate and a {ENTITY_ID} placeholder the user replaces with their LEI or registry identifier before submitting to a filing tool.

group.description: G-1700 — the GROUP batch. The route is chosen by the number of distinct entityIds on the items (items[i].input.entityId; an item without one belongs to accountingPolicy.entityId): ONE → that entity's separate statements; TWO OR MORE → consolidation, which REQUIRES this block (refused without it: several entities are consolidated only through a stated control relationship, IFRS 10.7). It is the IFRS 10 item's group facts in their own shapes (one element, one name): { parent: { entityId (= accountingPolicy.entityId), name }, entities: [{ entityId, name, heldBy (PARENT or an entityId), functionalCurrency, reportingDate (IFRS 10.B92 — equal to the parent's), acquisitionDate, ownershipInterest, controlFacts (IFRS 10.7, B14-B72), statementOfFinancialPositionAtAcquisitionDate or openingGoodwill + openingNonControllingInterest, investmentCarryingAmountInHolderStatements, ifrs3AcquisitionFacts, translation, … }], intragroupBalances, intragroupTransactions (entity ids on both sides) }. Each entity's statements (statementOfFinancialPositionAtReportingDate, comparativeStatementOfFinancialPosition, profitOrLoss, otherComprehensiveIncome, dividendsDeclared, equityTransactions) are DERIVED from its own items and its previousPeriodBalances rows (row.entity) — stating them is refused. Returns separateStatements[entityId] (each entity's own books, never holding a consolidation adjustment) and consolidated (the IFRS 10 statements and the consolidation journal entries, ledger CONSOLIDATION). The group statement of cash flows is DERIVED (direct method, IAS 7.19(a)): the sum of each entity's own cash lines less intragroup cash flows (IFRS 10.B86(c)); cashFlowFacts are not accepted (G-1724). DATED events (G-1720 / G-1721): every item is posted at its own input.reportingDate. A subsidiary acquired inside the period (acquisitionDate after previousReportingDate) enters the group from that date only (IFRS 10.20, B88): its statement at the acquisition date and its post-acquisition profit or loss, OCI and dividends are derived from its items dated up to / after it (an item dated ON the acquisition date is pre-acquisition); goodwill and the NCI come from ifrs3AcquisitionFacts. entities[].ownershipChanges[] (changeDate, ownershipInterestAfter, controlFactsAfter, consideration, considerationKind, gainRecognisedByHolder, investmentCarryingAmountInHolderStatementsAfter, retained-interest facts) — control retained → an equity transaction (IFRS 10.23; group.goodwillReallocationOnChangesInOwnershipInterest required), control lost → derecognition, the retained interest at fair value, the gain (IFRS 10.25, B98); the subsidiary's books on the change date (retainedEarningsAtChangeDate, otherComprehensiveIncomeBeforeChange, statementOfFinancialPositionAtDisposalDate) are derived — stating them is refused, as is statementOfFinancialPositionAtAcquisitionDate for an in-period acquisition. A subsidiary item other than a general-journal entry whose own period spans such a date is refused: split it there (never apportioned). A subsidiary's share issue reads the holder's subscription from its own postings on the issue date (G-1725); one subscribed out of proportion is stated as ownershipInterestAfter on an ownershipChanges row dated on the issue, its consideration derived (G-1976). The group cash flow statement takes a subsidiary acquired or lost inside the period from / until that date, the consideration net of the cash acquired or disposed of (IAS 7.39-42), and a subsidiary in another functional currency translated flow by flow, the effect of exchange rate changes apart (IAS 7.25-28) (G-1977). Associates and joint ventures with items are derived from them (IAS 28.10, IFRS 11.24): their profit and OCI from their own items, their dividends from the holder's dividend income on their declaration dates — those facts are never stated. Not built yet (refused, field named): a different subsidiary reporting date (B92-B93), a foreign associate or joint venture with items (IAS 21.44), a joint operation's items (IFRS 11.20-21 — post them in the operator's own items). An IFRS 10 item in a one-entity batch is refused — use this block.

includeDisclosureNotes.description: Default true. Set false to suppress the disclosureNotes key in the batch response (IFRS 18 aggregated disclosure notes).

includeWorkings.description: Default: false. When true, includes full per-item workings, disclosures, and journal entries (~3–10× larger response). When false (default), strips per-item workings, disclosures, step-by-step sections, and journal entries — every item's rows remain in the top-level batchJournalEntries array. Use false (default) for trial-balance and P&L analysis; use true only when you need step-by-step calculations per item.

includeXbrlEnrichment.description: Default: false. When true, includes the full xbrl metadata object on each journal entry debit/credit line (parentElement, label.hu, namespace, taxonomyYear, dimension, decimals — needed for iXBRL filing). When false (default), strips the nested xbrl object from DR/CR lines. The trial balance XBRL tags (xbrlElement, xbrlSection, xbrlLabel) are always preserved regardless of this setting.

finrepDimensions.description: OPTIONAL COMMONFINREP analytics dimensions for an ifrs9 item (the FINREP bridge workbook). Never read by the calculation.

counterpartySector.description: EBA FINREP Annex V counterparty sector of the instrument's counterparty — F 04 portfolio × sector pivot. Omitted items sit in "Unallocated".

productType.description: EBA FINREP F 05 product breakdown — F 05 loans by product pivot. Omitted items sit in "Unallocated".

input.description: Calculation input for this item — must include `id` alongside standard-specific fields.

mode.description: Default: "all-or-nothing" — if any item fails preflight validation the whole batch is rejected (no credits charged). Set to "partial" to skip the all-or-nothing gate: each item is validated-then-calculated independently; failed items return {status:"validation_error"|"calculation_error", error} while successful items return {status:"ok", result}; credits are only charged for items with status "ok". Partial mode returns per-item results ONLY — it does not assemble batchJournalEntries, trialBalance, financialStatements, cashFlowStatement, disclosureNotes or calculationSheetsUrl, and persists no workbook. For the consolidated statements and the download link, use the default mode.

previousPeriodBalances.description: The trial balance at previousReportingDate (G-1723: debit − credit; one entity's rows sum to 0, else refused before anything is calculated). When provided, the batch computes the closing statement of financial position: closing per account = opening + the period's net movement (debit − credit), and the period's profit or loss and OCI are closed to equity. crossChecks.closingSOFP gives closingAssets / closingLiabilities / closingEquity (presented, positive), profitForPeriod, otherComprehensiveIncome, equationGap (= assets − liabilities − equity, 0 on a balanced opening) and byAccount (opening / periodNet / closing, debit − credit); crossChecks.sofpIsFullyBalanced = true when the equation holds. The same rows make each XBRL instant fact a closing balance. They are not needed for financialStatements.statementOfFinancialPosition, which is the PERIOD DELTA of each line derived from the batch's own postings (G-1871, owner 2026-10-05).

account.description: Account name — the account as the journal entries post it. A general-journal vocabulary spelling (e.g. "Accounts Payable") or another case is read on the published name ("Trade and Other Payables") (G-2237).

balance.description: G-1723 — the balance at previousReportingDate in the LEDGER's sign convention: debit − credit. An asset is positive; a liability or an equity balance is NEGATIVE (a contra-asset such as accumulated depreciation is negative too). The rows of one entity sum to 0 — a balanced trial balance is a fact you state; an unbalanced set is refused naming the difference, nothing is plugged.

entity.description: G-1700 — the entityId whose balance this is. REQUIRED on every row of a group batch (items of two or more entities): each entity's run receives its own rows, and its rows sum to 0 on their own.

xbrlSection.description: XBRL section of the account: Assets | Liabilities | Equity. An opening balance is a statement-of-financial-position balance — PL, OCI and CashFlow rows are refused (the previous period's profit or loss and OCI are already in retained earnings and the reserves, IAS 1.106(d)). `BalanceSheet` and `IncomeStatement` are STATEMENT names, not sections, and are rejected (G-192).

supplierFinanceArrangements.description: G-2301 — REQUIRED when any general-journal line of the batch states supplierFinanceArrangementId (refused otherwise, field by field): one row per supplier finance arrangement (IAS 7.44G), its terms stated once. Every row must describe an arrangement a line references. The batch then publishes cashFlowStatement.data.supplierFinanceArrangements: IAS 7.44H(a) terms by group of similar terms (extended payment terms and early payment derived from the items' dates), (b)(i)-(iii) the carrying amounts and line items, the part suppliers were already paid and the payment-due-date ranges (with comparable trade payables from the ordinary supplier payments' invoiceDate / invoiceDueDate) at the beginning and end of the period, (c) the non-cash changes by type, and the IFRS 7.39(a) / B11F(j) liquidity-risk facts.

securityOrGuaranteeProvided.description: IAS 7.44H(a) — the security or guarantees provided under the arrangement: NONE, SECURITY_OVER_ASSETS, GUARANTEE_BY_GROUP_ENTITY, GUARANTEE_BY_THIRD_PARTY or SECURITY_AND_GUARANTEE. Never assumed.

supplierFinanceArrangementId.description: The arrangement, as its general-journal arrangement lines state it (entries[i].supplierFinanceArrangementId).

name: ifr_period_end_batch
